title: Trial drift pocket log — kenji
content:
Purpose: quick personal tracker for a small series of micro-bench runs focused on observing latency/cost drift across long-lived KV-cache usage and bursty traffic. Not a polished report — iterative notes + tiny table to copy into Confluence later.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Drift appears when sequence-length distribution shifts to longer prefixes and KV cache hit ratio falls below ~0.6 for this workload. Expect >12% p95 latency increase and ~8% token-cost rise due to extra compute per token.

Metadata
- model: llama-2-13b-v1-fp16 (quantized-step: q4f16)
- infra: dedicated-pool-east-1 (A100s), pod-type: 1xA100-80GB
- warmup policy: prefix-cache-warm (30s prefill)
- commit: serving-runtime@7c3a2b4

Mini table (rows = runs). Columns: run_id, start, duration, batch_size, seq_mean, kv_hit_pct, tok/s, p50(ms), p95(ms), cost_per_1k_tok, notes

R1, 2025-02-07T09:12, 00:45, 8, 256, 0.82, 14,200, 42, 87, $0.62, baseline steady, low jitter
R2, 2025-02-07T11:03, 00:38, 8, 288, 0.71, 12,900, 46, 103, $0.68, slight drift after 18m (kv hit drop)
R3, 2025-02-08T02:17, 01:20, 16, 200, 0.55, 17,400, 60, 135, $0.74, bursty tails; p95 noisy; peak tok/s good
R4, 2025-02-09T22:05, 00:30, 8, 320, 0.48, 11,800, 70, 158, $0.80, long prefixes -> high p95, cost up
R5, 2025-02-11T07:40, 00:50, 4, 128, 0.91, 8,300, 30, 65, $0.55, small batch, high cache -> cheapest

Quick observations (raw):
- KV-hit below ~0.6 correlates strongly with p95 ballooning. Example: R2->R4 shift where hit% 0.71 -> 0.48 produced p95 103 -> 158 ms.
- Batch size trade: R3 (batch=16) increased tok/s but p95 worse when kv-hit low. For latency SLO we prefer smaller batch when cache unstable.
- Cost delta between best/worst ~45% across these runs (per-1k token).

Mini calc notes:
- approximate token cost formula used: run_cost_est = (gpu_minute_rate * minutes) / (total_tokens / 1000). Using A100 rate ~= $2.1/min for this pool (internal estimate).
- Example R4: minutes=0.5 -> $1.05; total_tokens ~= tok/s * 30s? (rough) -> noisy; these are quick eyeball numbers, not billed values.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run R4 with prefix-adaptive-cache (reduce cache eviction) to see effect on kv_hit_pct and p95.
- [ ] Add instrumentation to emit KV eviction rate per minute (current metric not available in the pipeline). Filed INF-2048 but need a short PR to hook the exporter.
- [ ] Try per-request early-fallback to smaller batch when measured kv_hit < 0.6 for last 60s (policy experiment).
- [ ] Save a longer run (4h) overnight with low-intensity traffic; collect drift curve and per-minute tok/s.

Notes to self / random scribbles:
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (see thread pinned message "kv-cache patterns")
- Possible confounder: model quantization step (q4f16) might interact with kernel selection and produce different perf when seq_len>300. Add a quick q3 test.
- If billing precision needed, pluck exact pod-minutes from Usage API for the experiment window.

Short checklist for next run:
1) flip exporter flag (kv-evictions=true) -> INF-2048
2) schedule 4h run from 02:00->06:00 local test window
3) baseline sample at start (30s steady traffic)
4) switch traffic to long-prefix distribution (simulate user multi-turn) at t=+45m
5) capture logs + attach to PR 789 for trace examples

Scratch math (hand):
- If tok/s=11,800 and run 30s -> total tokens ~= 354k -> cost ~ ($2.1 * 0.5) / (354k/1000) ~= $1.05 / 354 ~= $0.00297 per 1k? (this indicates my earlier per-1k numbers are ballpark; need to recompute with exact usage).

Final quick note: keep this sheet as my working log. When we have the exporter data, convert to a proper CSV and push to /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks/ with a small README.

End of scratch.
